Although we share in the ACHP's concern for all historic sites on or eligible for the National Register of Historic Places, we would specifically mention the following for their related status:
The Dilloway-Thomas House (on John Eliot Square, Roxbury) which is under continued study by Congressional request as being a possible addition to the Boston National Historical Park (P.L. 93-431).
The Shirley-Eustis House (Roxbury) and William Lloyd Garrison House (Roxbury) which are National Historic Landmarks as well as being listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
If there should be any alteration or expansion of the work areas for building clearance in South Boston, then Dorchester Heights National Historic Site may be affected. This National Historic Site is also being studied for possible inclusion in the Boston National Historic Park (P.L. 93-431).
Further, the environmental statement indicates the need for immediate implementation of measures to control erosion on cleared steep sites (p. 101). This should be expanded to discuss protective measures to minimize erosion from all cleared sites in the project area. The statement should also mention the need for properly sealing all wells, cisterns, or other excavations through which pollution might gain fairly direct access to the ground-water reservoir.
In addition to rodent control proposed for the demolition areas (p. 104), consideration should be given to problems that may exist or be caused by the common pigeon. These birds have a tendency to take up residence in abandoned buildings. If during the course of demolition large numbers of these birds are displaced, they could easily cause problems in the surrounding buildings and neighborhoods in an attempt to find new roost sites. We would suggest that if during the rodent control survey large populations of pigeons are observed, plans should be made for their elimination in addition to rodent extermination.
We would be pleased to see the final environmental statement containing these suggested areas of concern so that this proposal can be accomplished as beneficially as possible for all parties affected.
Sincerely yours,
Roger Sumner Babb
Special Assistant to
the Secretary
